title: The great tongue (Kern ch. 20)
hookLine: the Buddhas show their power to confirm the teaching

lines: A STAMP, A HANDSHAKE, A SIGNATURE.
THE BUDDHAS PUT OUT THEIR TONGUES.
cards: A notary's stamp. A handshake in front of witnesses. A signature on the line.
People have many ways of saying: this counts, and I stand behind it. Chapter twenty of the Lotus Sutra, in Kern's numbering, has one of its own. The Buddhas put out their tongues.
It sounds almost comic at first, and it is meant to be enormous. It's also the last day of this week, so after the scene, the week's lines get gathered up.

teach.b: First, the scene. The bodhisattvas who rose from the cracks of the earth have just vowed to carry the teaching after the Buddha is gone.
Then Shakyamuni, the ancient Buddha Prabhutaratna seated beside him in the jeweled stupa, and all the Buddhas gathered from other worlds, each on a lion seat, put out their tongues.

The tongues reach up to the Brahma heaven, and rays of light pour from them. Tradition says a long, broad tongue is one of a Buddha's bodily marks, the sign of a speaker who does not lie. So the gesture isn't rude.
It means: what was said here is true. Second, the sound.

teach.h: A COUGH, A SNAP, WORLDS HEAR.
teach.b: Then the Buddhas clear their throats and snap their fingers, all together, and the sound reaches worlds in every direction. Beings everywhere look up, see the great assembly, and are glad. Third, the handing over.
With the teaching confirmed, the Buddha entrusts it to the bodhisattvas.

teach.h: ANY PLACE CAN BE THE SEAT.
teach.b: Wherever it is kept, read or explained, in a park or a forest, under a tree, in a monastery or a family's house, that spot is to be honored as the place where Buddhas awaken.
Look back at the lines you've carried: always here, take the medicine, glad news, passed on and on, clear senses, I do not despise you.
Each came from a chapter of this sutra, and today the sutra puts its own stamp on the whole book, with a gesture as wide as the worlds.

how: Schools that center the Lotus Sutra read this chapter as the Buddhas' confirmation of the teaching and its handing over to the bodhisattvas, and honor the places where the sutra is kept and practiced.

o: the Buddhas' tongues reaching heaven: this teaching is true
a gift of speech given to the newest bodhisattvas
a sign of mockery the crowd makes at the Buddha

s: in this chapter the Buddhas' tongues reach up to the Brahma heaven
and rays of light shine from them, confirming the teaching.
putting out the tongue is meant as mockery in this scene
tradition says a long, broad tongue is the mark of a speaker who does not lie.
the chapter says only temples may be honored as places of awakening
it names parks, forests, the foot of a tree, monasteries and family houses.

games.q: the teaching has been given. the bodhisattvas from the earth have vowed to carry it on. what do the Buddhas do next?
o: put out their tongues, clear their throats and snap their fingers
test the bodhisattvas one by one
games.why: the Buddhas confirm the teaching with tongues reaching the heavens and a sound heard in every world, then entrust it to the bodhisattvas.

practice: Look back for one kind thing you said recently that hasn't been backed up yet: let's get coffee, I'll call you, I'm here if you need anything.
Hold it for a few breaths, and let one small action come into view that would make it true, a time, a message, a step out the door. You don't have to do it now; just let the breath rest around it.

wordCard.voice: The great tongue. In the Lotus Sutra, the Buddhas' tongues reaching the heavens, a sign that the teaching is true and confirmed. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: tongue; in this chapter the Buddhas' tongues reach the Brahma heaven.
